method.title: How prices work
method.lead: Everything this site shows comes from a dated reading. This page says which reading, when it was taken, and what we refuse to count.
method.floor.p1: The floor is the lowest listing on sale at the moment of the reading. It is not an estimate and not a model: it is a price someone is asking, at a precise time.
method.floor.p2: A single listing is enough to carry it — which also means it can vanish with the next sale. A floor describes an offer, never a settled value.
method.excluded.p1: Some floors describe a seller rather than a market: one isolated listing at a joke price would be enough to distort a ranking. A check keeps those out of the rankings. It never looks at the price on its own — it weighs what the item is usually worth, how many listings actually hold that floor up, and what the item's own record says. An expensive piece with a long history defends itself; an expensive piece that appeared overnight, with nobody behind it, does not.
method.excluded.count: {n} items out of {total} are flagged today.
method.excluded.p2: They stay visible and keep their displayed price, marked as unrepresentative. We flag, we never hide — it is the rankings that leave them out.
method.h.markets: The two markets are never merged
method.markets.p1: Prices come from two separate places. The VeVe market is denominated in dollars; StackR, a third-party venue, is denominated in the OMI token. The same piece is a different number on each.
method.markets.p2: Adding them together would produce a figure that means nothing. They are read separately, shown separately, and every amount carries the market it came from.
method.rate.p1: When an amount in OMI has to be read in dollars, the conversion uses the rate from the day of the sale, not today's rate — otherwise a sale from last year would change value every morning. The rate and its date are shown next to the converted amount, so the calculation can be redone.
